Graphden stores program composition as data: which function specializes which parent, and where each input comes from. Small Clojure primitives provide the operations; the graph connects them. This makes reuse, dependencies, types, and branch-specific changes visible to the editor and executor. See the [[file:../../../docs/PHILOSOPHY.md][design rationale]].

This tour explains how Graphden stores, compiles, and runs [[file:glossary.org::#term/graph-function][graph functions]]. It assumes basic Clojure and HTTP knowledge. A [[file:glossary.org::#term/graph-function][graph function]] describes a computation; an [[file:glossary.org::#term/slot][argument slot]] identifies one input, and a [[file:glossary.org::#term/binding][binding]] supplies that input. An [[file:glossary.org::#term/context][execution context]] selects storage, branch, caches, and execution policy. A [[file:glossary.org::#term/compiled-registry][compiled registry]] maps function IDs to callable Clojure [[file:glossary.org::#term/closure][closures]]. Follow a linked term whenever you need its definition; definitions are outside the numbered steps and do not change reading progress.

Start with Executor for a worked composition and its execution path. Packages explains the source files that author that graph; Graph API and Editor connect it to a user's edit. The [[file:../../../docs/devtour/README.md][reading routes and first change]] give a shorter path through these mechanisms before you explore every block.

Read the blocks in [[file:glossary.org::#term/topological-order][dependency order]], starting with Executor. Boot is also a useful starting point if you want to understand process startup first. The Editor block reads JavaScript; the other blocks primarily read Clojure. The user-facing editor lessons are separate from this developer tour.

Every step displays actual source from a named form. See-also links open related steps, and Back returns along your navigation path. Definition links open a separate reference view; in Emacs, Return to the tour closes its help window.

The same source generates this standalone page, the Emacs data, and the Org reading files. See [[file:../../../docs/devtour/README.md][setup]]. For build, tests, isolated worktrees, and the merge queue, read [[file:../../../CLAUDE.md][CLAUDE.md]] and [[file:../../../dev/wtq/AGENT.md][worktree workflow]].
